races.name: Betfair Backs Opinions Superior Mile Stakes (Group 3)

runners_data.name: Balmacara
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist who has shown ability over 7f-8f on soft/good-to-soft, stepping up here for Eve Johnson Houghton after 63 days off; the Heavy ground is not a concern based on similar-going record (9 placings from 15), and Callum Hutchinson's claim could matter in a stamina test.|

runners_data.name: Dancing Gemini
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride for Roger Teal on this hold-up performer who has struggled to convert on Good ground lately (four runs, no win at 8-10f on Good); similar-going stats are modest but Heavy may genuinely suit this horse better than its recent form suggests, and headgear (p) worn previously may be notable.|

runners_data.name: Fondo Blanco
runners_data.note: Roger Varian's four-year-old ran only seven days ago — significant on Heavy ground — and shows two wins and strong placed form on Soft/Soft-Heavy going; Ray Dawson rides and this horse's natural race from a prominent position will be tested by the congested early exchanges.|

runners_data.name: Persica
runners_data.note: Consistent and classy — won at 10f on Good and placed at Group level on Soft — but Richard Hannon's stable is 0 from 45 over the last 14 days, a significant negative; James Doyle's experience in big fields on testing ground is an asset, and Persica's genuine prominence style gives a strong positional platform.|

runners_data.name: The Lost King
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on Soft and Good for Andrew Balding, with PJ McDonald aboard, and only one run on similar Heavy-type going (1 win from 13), which is the key query; youth (four-year-old) and form trajectory are positive, but the stamina question on punishing Heavy ground over a mile is real.|

runners_data.name: Colori Forever
runners_data.note: Three-year-old carrying a 5lb age allowance and with wins at 7f on Good and Soft conditions for Marco Botti; similar-going stats are limited (1 placing from 8, no wins), and after 58 days off, fitness and the step into Group company on the worst ground of the day are significant risk factors.|

runners_data.name: Hankelow
runners_data.note: K.R. Burke's three-year-old is a confirmed front-runner who was placed on Heavy ground three runs ago and is 8/41 for the trainer over 14 days; the back-to-back lead with Needle Match is the headline concern — if Clifford Lee goes too hard early the Heavy ground will find him out emphatically.|

runners_data.name: Needle Match
runners_data.note: William Haggas's three-year-old returned with a place last time after winning on Soft debut, and Tom Marquand will look to exploit natural front-running style; limited similar-going data (one win from four on Soft) leaves genuine uncertainty about whether this horse truly stays a mile in Heavy conditions under pressure.|

runners_data.name: Redemption Road
runners_data.note: Michael Keady's three-year-old has been placed three times on Soft and Good-to-Soft and is clearly a hold-up type drawn toward the closing stages; the 86-day absence is the biggest concern, and the trainer's quiet recent figures (0/11 over 14 days) do nothing to encourage confidence on a day with this ground.|

races.paceDynamic: Hankelow and Needle Match are both confirmed front-runners and will contest the lead from the off over Haydock's flat mile on testing Heavy ground, creating a genuinely contested early gallop rather than a soft-pedal lead. Four of the nine runners — Fondo Blanco, Persica, The Lost King, and Colori Forever — all want prominent positions, meaning the first two furlongs will see significant jostling for berths, with real traffic danger and interference likely between the 2f and 3f poles as they bunch around the turn. On Heavy ground at Haydock over a mile, a contested pace almost invariably produces a genuine, end-to-end test of stamina where the fractions are honest enough to suit those able to settle just off the pace and finish powerfully. This race shape strongly favours hold-up horses with genuine Heavy-ground form and the class to pick off a tiring field in the final two furlongs, with the prominent wall likely to over-race early and pay for it.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Pace, Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Hankelow and Needle Match burn each other up through a genuine Heavy-ground gallop, leaving tiring bodies across the home straight.
scenarios.body: The dual front-runner duel burns through the field quickly on punishing ground, opening the race up for hold-up types to weave through spent rivals in the final two furlongs; Haydock's flat finish rewards those who have conserved energy until the turn.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Runners Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuine but not suicidal, allowing an organised prominent runner to settle just behind the leaders and produce a sustained, staying finish.
scenarios.body: A horse like Persica or The Lost King — both with strong recent form and capable of sitting comfortably in third or fourth — gets the perfect stalking position and hits the front at the right moment on softening ground; The Lost King's consecutive wins on Soft and Good give him the profile, while Persica's recent Group-level placed form underlines class.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Hankelow or Needle Match seizes an uncontested or easier-than-expected lead early and dictates a controlled tempo that kills off rivals without burning themselves out.
scenarios.body: On Heavy ground a disciplined front-runner who avoids a furious early duel can find a rhythm that is lethal to hold-up horses giving away too much ground; Hankelow's Heavy-ground third and Needle Match's experience at the trip give each a platform if the other capitulates or settles early.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Produces Big-Field Shake-Up
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes interference, bumping, or mis-steps on heavy ground between the 6f and 4f poles that disrupts the majority of the field.
scenarios.body: A bunched field on punishing going with four horses all demanding prominent positions is a recipe for a compressed, chaotic mid-race, potentially stopping the momentum of the fancied runners and opening the door for a runner on the outer or one who avoids trouble entirely.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion between Fondo Blanco, Persica, The Lost King, and Colori Forever could cause early bumping or interference — watch the first two furlongs closely as all four seek the same berths behind Hankelow and Needle Match.

Hankelow and Needle Match duelling for the lead on Heavy ground risks a pace collapse — if either goes too hard in front the race may become a test of survival rather than tactical racing, favouring hold-up horses who settle furthest back.

Fondo Blanco ran just seven days ago — horses returning quickly on Heavy ground are at elevated risk of fatigue late, and Ray Dawson will need to judge pace perfectly from a prominent position to avoid the horse emptying out in the final furlong.

Dancing Gemini's recent form on Good ground is uninspiring but William Buick's tactical intelligence from a hold-up position could prove decisive if the front-runners and prominent brigade collectively tie each other up.

The Lost King's single similar-going run (1 win from 13 on Heavy-adjacent ground) is a thin sample — Andrew Balding and PJ McDonald are strong pointers, but the stamina question on this ground at a mile deserves monitoring in the parade ring for any signs of physical stress.

races.name: Betfair Celebrates Bow Echo Ascendant Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: Arthurian
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's colt is a confirmed front-runner who will attempt to make the running from the outset, but finishing sixth last time out at Goodwood on good ground is concerning, and sharing pace duties with two rivals on heavy going makes his chance of lasting out the mile fraught.|

runners_data.name: First Law
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby and William Buick represent the gold standard combination, and First Law arrives on the back of a Goodwood win, but that sole start on good ground leaves his heavy going credentials genuinely untested — a significant concern over a stamina-sapping Haydock mile.|

runners_data.name: Rafe's Da Man
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's prominent racer has shown consistency in defeat with placed efforts on good ground at Goodwood, and the step up to a genuinely stamina-testing mile in heavy conditions may suit a horse whose form string shows progressive improvement; Levey's positioning skills behind a hot pace are an asset.|

runners_data.name: Rocket Boy
runners_data.note: Marco Botti's colt won over 7f at Goodwood and is a natural front-runner who will press for the lead alongside First Law and Arthurian, but contesting a three-way pace battle on heavy ground represents a formidable physical ask and risks him emptying well before the line.|

runners_data.name: Romanza
runners_data.note: Charlie Fellowes' filly has placed experience on both good and soft-ish ground and comes with headgear (noted), suggesting she benefits from assistance in focus; her prominent style means she could slot just off the warring leaders and stay on if they capitulate, though her OR of 85 represents a steep class jump.|

runners_data.name: Theheatison
runners_data.note: Nick Scholfield's hold-up performer arrives most recently from a second over 7f on soft ground, which is the most relevant form on the card for today's conditions; the sharp class rise into Listed company is the primary obstacle, but the running style is perfectly mapped for a race where three leaders are likely to combust.|

races.paceDynamic: Three confirmed front-runners — Arthurian, First Law, and Rocket Boy — guarantee an aggressive pace from the off on heavy ground at Haydock, creating a severe stamina examination over a flat mile. Buick on First Law (OR 120, sole win on good) and Ghiani on Rocket Boy will both attempt to press from the front, with Balding's Arthurian equally unlikely to surrender early, meaning the early fractions will be contested rather than controlled. This internecine battle between three two-year-olds on testing heavy ground will drain reserves rapidly and leave the pace-setters vulnerable in the final two furlongs. The race shape strongly favours hold-up and prominent runners who can settle off the war, time their move, and sustain it through the testing ground — making Romanza and Rafe's Da Man the profile beneficiaries, with Theheatison's hold-up style also well positioned if the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace War Drains Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If all three front-runners — Arthurian, First Law, Rocket Boy — contest the lead through the first half and burn each other out on heavy ground.
scenarios.body: The relentless early fractions in testing conditions will see the front trio cry enough in the final quarter-mile, leaving prominent and hold-up runners to sweep through their tiring bodies. Rafe's Da Man and Romanza, both settled in the early stages, are the primary profile beneficiaries here as they arrive with energy intact.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Buick Controls, Kicks Clear
scenarios.trigger: If William Buick on First Law uses class and experience to establish a controlled solo lead and dictates a sensible pace that preserves his horse's stamina.
scenarios.body: First Law's Appleby team connection and Buick's tactical intelligence could mean he simply outwits the other two pace-setters and settles into a rhythm that renders the race manageable rather than a slog. With a Goodwood win already on his card and an OR of 120, he has the class to dominate if given even a fraction of daylight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Storm Home Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly suicidal and all three front-runners capitulate, allowing hold-up runner Theheatison to benefit from maximum late energy.
scenarios.body: Theheatison's hold-up style suits a race that becomes a rout at the front, and the horse has course-relevant experience on soft-to-heavy variants with recent form suggesting stamina is present. However, the horse steps up sharply in class at Listed level and Donohoe riding a winner from the back on this track requires everything to go right.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Shock Prominent Run Wins
scenarios.trigger: If one of the lower-rated prominent or lead types — Romanza or Rocket Boy — secures a comfortable early position at a more sedate pace and outstays rivals.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires the contest between front-runners to settle unusually quickly and one to dictate without serious challenge, which is unlikely with three confirmed leaders and heavy ground. Romanza has headgear notation and ran well to place at Newmarket over 7f, so possesses a residual chance if race shape falls kindly.

watchPoints.text: Monitor First Law's early behaviour under Buick — if he slots in behind rather than leads, the front-running trio shrinks to two and the tempo could ease enough to give the pace-setters a fighting chance.

Watch Rocket Boy's position in the first furlong — if he and Arthurian both press First Law hard into the first bend, the three-way duel on heavy Haydock ground will almost certainly result in none of them lasting the mile.

Theheatison has 1W 1P from 6 runs on similar going and arrives just 16 days since last run — check pre-race condition and market moves as trainer Nick Scholfield is 2/15 over the past 14 days, giving this a marginal operational angle.
Romanza's headgear noted — confirm she is wearing it today; if it sharpens her early response she may travel better than her OR suggests and secure a prominent pitch just off the chaos ahead.

Heavy ground is confirmed across the card all day at Haydock — no easing expected, meaning the stamina test will only intensify as the afternoon progresses; any horse with a going concern on soft-heavy should be downgraded further at the off.

races.name: Best Odds On The Betfair Exchange Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Galilean Quality
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with heavy-ground form flags and a 14-day turnaround for the in-form Burke yard; maps perfectly for this race shape and dictates everything from the front, though her best form has come at 12f and this step to 14f on testing ground is worth monitoring in the final stages.

runners_data.name: Mythical Bay
runners_data.note: Tudhope pairs up with the Balding yard in the most prominent tracking position, and her form at 14f on soft ground is directly relevant — she is a natural traveller who can sit close to the pace and mount a sustained challenge in the straight without burning her reserves.

runners_data.name: Pierre Grosse
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up operator for the Harrington yard who has placed twice over 13f on soft and twice over 12f on good, but this 14f heavy test is new territory; Kennedy takes the 5lb claim and the extra yardage may actually help if the stamina test is severe, though 28 days off and limited similar-going experience temper expectations.

runners_data.name: Asia Force
runners_data.note: Buick's booking is the eye-catcher here, and Asia Force is a natural hold-up horse with a win at 14f on good; displaced into the midfield mapping because the field is loaded with hold-up types, she will be racing slightly ahead of her preferred position and her chance is therefore harder to realise than the jockey booking implies.

runners_data.name: Lopeo
runners_data.note: Menuisier's 63-day freshener is notable but his one heavy-ground run produced a win at 8f, and this 14f trip on a true stamina test is the most extreme combination of conditions he has faced; a genuine stay-on type whose form over 14f on good at Goodwood is encouraging, making him the most interesting of the hold-up profile horses if the pace quickens.

runners_data.name: Reem Rak
runners_data.note: Varian's yard is in fair form over the 14-day window, and Reem Rak has both won and placed at 14f — but she is a true hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield mapping position by the density of closers in this field, meaning Dawson will need a perfect run through horses that aren't naturally in front of her.

runners_data.name: Bridge Of Eagles
runners_data.note: Has finished placed twice in her last two starts and shapes as a genuine prominent-position runner who stays further than her 10f form suggests; steps up substantially in trip here and on the most testing ground she has faced, and while the style suits the race shape, the combination of trip and going is an unknown.

runners_data.name: Cotton Bud
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer whose natural position at the front of the pace group is congested here; Lycett's yard has had limited recent runners and Cotton Bud's best effort was a win at 10f on good, making both the trip extension to 14f and the heavy ground significant untested factors — the style may get her close early but stamina is the question.

races.paceDynamic: Galilean Quality is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field over 1m6f on heavy ground at Haydock, and with no genuine pace rival to pressure her, she is set to control tempo from the outset at a rate entirely of her own choosing. Mythical Bay and Bridge Of Eagles will look to track closely in a prominent position, but with the pace undisturbed, the gallop is unlikely to be severe enough to string the field out early — a steady-to-moderate tempo over this trip on heavy ground can compress the race into a late test of stamina and resolution. Cotton Bud, Asia Force, and Reem Rak are all genuine prominent or hold-up types who cannot all secure their natural position in this field shape; Cotton Bud is the most likely of the three to push forward toward the front, while Asia Force and Reem Rak will be operating further back than suits them. With one unchallenged pace-setter dictating from the front over a stamina-sapping 1m6f on heavy going, this race shape most strongly favours horses that can race prominently without expending energy in the early stages, travel smoothly into the straight, and sustain their effort through the demanding ground — a clean trip close to the pace is the decisive tactical advantage here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Galilean Quality Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Galilean Quality dictates an uncontested, measured tempo and those tracking her cannot quicken past when the race unfolds.
scenarios.body: Galilean Quality sets a sustainable fractions on heavy ground, conserving enough energy to repel challengers in the final two furlongs as the stamina test intensifies; Mythical Bay, tracking prominently from early, is best placed to mount the closest pursuit given her class and prominent profile.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Wear Down Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Mythical Bay or Bridge Of Eagles sit close enough to Galilean Quality to pounce decisively in the straight when the heavy ground extracts its toll.
scenarios.body: The steady early pace means the race turns into a stamina duel from the home turn, and a horse that has sat two lengths off the leader without burning energy has the ideal platform; Mythical Bay's class and Tudhope's experience of these conditions makes her the most dangerous challenger in this shape.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Stamina Grinder From Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the pace quickens sufficiently early to string the field, allowing a genuine stayer tracking midfield to pick off tiring rivals in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Lopeo has heavy-ground form and stays well, and if the fractions are stronger than anticipated he can close from midfield as the field exhausts itself in the final furlong; Pierre Grosse also has the staying profile to benefit from a true-run stamina contest at this trip.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Cause Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the race collapses into a falsely slow early pace and a sprint finish that negates stamina, allowing hold-up horses to arrive late with momentum.
scenarios.body: Asia Force and Reem Rak are genuine hold-up types displaced into midfield mapping positions, and a truly falsely-run race over this trip is the only scenario in which they can meaningfully threaten; however, their redistributed positions and the difficulty of making significant late ground on heavy going at Haydock over 1m6f makes this an unlikely outcome.

watchPoints.text: Galilean Quality is the only horse who can dictate tempo entirely on her own terms — if she gets a clear lead within the first two furlongs and settles into a rhythm, she will be very hard to dislodge in the straight given how heavy ground rewards conserved energy.

William Buick's booking for Asia Force is a significant market signal — watch for her drifting or firming in the market, as any significant move could indicate stable confidence in a horse whose true hold-up style is compromised by the field shape.

Lopeo and Bridge Of Eagles share the same 63-day layoff from the Menuisier yard and are drawn together in terms of prep; watch whether one or both ease in the market, as a deliberate tactical targeting of this race by the trainer could be significant.

Pierre Grosse, Reem Rak, and Asia Force are all genuine hold-up horses operating in a race with limited room at the rear — monitor early running to see whether any of them are forced wider or forced to cover more ground than anticipated in a compressed midfield on a testing surface.

The heavy ground at Haydock over 1m6f will be a stamina examination unlike anything most of this field has faced — check which runners have the most directly relevant similar-going form entries in their history, as the sim-going figures across this field are uniformly low (1/6 to 3/9), meaning the surface is a genuine equaliser.

races.name: Betfair Exchange Old Borough Cup Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Aegean Prince
runners_data.note: 320 days off the track for Charlie Appleby is the obvious flag — but he won on Heavy and has soft-ground form; if Buick gets a clean prominent pitch just off Finalise, his class could mask any rustiness over this stamina test.

runners_data.name: Stressfree
runners_data.note: Ran 14 days ago and has shown nothing lately (form reads 27086), with zero wins or places from 15 similar-going starts — a genuine hold-up type but needs dramatic improvement in form on what is clearly a difficult surface for him.

runners_data.name: Valedictory
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's four-year-old has winning form over 14f on Good but has not yet demonstrated he handles truly Heavy conditions; James Doyle will aim for a prominent pitch and his class warrants respect if he handles the ground.

runners_data.name: Dancing In Paris
runners_data.note: Won over this exact 16f trip at Goodwood in good ground but his soft/heavy record is thin — Ian Williams keeps him prominently, yet three wins from 15 similar-going starts is hardly a ringing endorsement of his mud credentials.

runners_data.name: In The Breeze
runners_data.note: Henrietta Knight's eight-year-old has four wins and four places from six similar-going starts — the standout Heavy-ground profiler in this field — and his two wins over 16f show the trip is no obstacle; Ray Dawson rides a hold-up horse with genuine stamina credentials.

runners_data.name: Mountain Road
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's seven-year-old has placed in his last two over this exact 16f trip at Goodwood and won the 16f at Goodwood earlier in the season — a natural prominent runner on a surface that suits grinding types who stay every yard.

runners_data.name: Finalise
runners_data.note: William Haggas's sole front-runner faces no pace pressure whatsoever, giving Marquand total control of the race; his Heavy form is limited but the unchallenged lead on 1m6f in this field is a structural advantage that transcends any going concern.

runners_data.name: Synergism
runners_data.note: Sir Mark Prescott's four-year-old wears a hood and has placed in three of his last four over 14-16f on softer surfaces — maps to a prominent role that should be achievable in this field and his yard's patience with staying types is well noted.

runners_data.name: Ashnak
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old has two wins and three places from nine similar-going runs, suggesting adequate if not exceptional Heavy-ground form; Daniel Tudhope will push for a prominent position but the 42-day absence and a form string of 83427 make him hard to fancy at the business end.

runners_data.name: Pole Star
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old naturally wants to race prominently — he wears a hood and has one win from two similar-ground outings — but in a field this stacked with prominent types he is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal, which materially undermines his chance.

runners_data.name: Hermetic
runners_data.note: Ian Williams's four-year-old has finished fourth in four of his last five starts at similar trips — consistent but unable to win — and though he genuinely wants to race prominently, the depth of the prominent queue here means he will almost certainly race in midfield against his instincts, diluting whatever chance he holds.

runners_data.name: Glen To Glen
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on Good ground and has a Heavy-ground point in his history — handles staying trips — but a form string of 297-09 and Stevie Donohoe's booking from a small yard suggest he is very much a fringe player today.

runners_data.name: Kissmehoneyhoney
runners_data.note: Only three runs on record for Haggas, including a win on soft and a second on Good — a filly who naturally wants to race prominently, though in this overloaded prominent tier she is almost certain to find herself shuffled into midfield, compromising a profile that depends on a forward berth.

runners_data.name: Golden West
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's five-year-old has zero wins or places from 11 similar-going starts — the worst Heavy-ground profile in the field — and while Duran Fentiman can drop him in from the hold-up position, there is very little evidence he can deliver on this surface over this trip.

races.paceDynamic: Finalise is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 14-strong field and, with no rival likely to seriously challenge for the lead, Tom Marquand can dictate a measured, unchallenged gallop on genuinely Heavy ground over 1m6f — conditions that will make every furlong feel like two. Behind him, Aegean Prince, Valedictory, Dancing In Paris, Mountain Road, Synergism, and Ashnak all want prominent positions, creating a congested queue for the berths just off the pace that will force several to race wider or further back than ideal from the 2-3f marker inward. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can realistically be accommodated in the first rank; Pole Star, Hermetic, and Kissmehoneyhoney are the ones most likely to be squeezed out of their natural position and end up racing in midfield against their instincts. On Heavy ground over this stamina-sapping trip, with a single unchallenged leader setting a sustainable but grinding tempo, the race shape heavily favours proven stayers who can travel prominently just behind the pace and sustain their effort through the testing closing stages — free-moving hold-up types who depend on a genuine sprint finish are at a structural disadvantage today.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Finalise Dictates, Stayers Strike
scenarios.trigger: If Finalise bowls along unchallenged and the prominent pack burns itself out fighting for position, leaving the truest stayers to come through late.
scenarios.body: Finalise sets a rhythm that suits his own profile while the prominent scramble for slots 2-6 uses up horses on the demanding surface; the winner emerges from those who travelled economically just behind or from genuine hold-up stayers who find the pace tempo just right for a sustained late run.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Survivor Grinds Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one of the better-credentialled prominent types secures a clean position close to Finalise and simply outstays rivals on the Heavy ground.
scenarios.body: With the pace controlled and non-threatening, a horse like Valedictory or Aegean Prince that locks onto Finalise's quarters without burning energy in the early jostling can hit the front 2f out and grind home on a surface that rewards class and stamina over raw speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely testing enough to string the field out and a true hold-up runner threads through a tiring pack in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Heavy ground over 1m6f can produce a genuine stamina test that rewards a horse dropped right out early, but this scenario is tempered by the fact that several apparent hold-up runners in this field are redistributed prominent types who lack true late-running gears.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Chaos Reigns
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent congestion causes a traffic incident 3f out or Finalise's pace is too slow, causing a sprint finish on testing ground.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race on Heavy going would theoretically suit a horse with a finishing kick, but with redistributed prominent types likely to be shuffled backward the scenario is structurally unlikely and the horses who would benefit from it are not well-represented by genuine hold-up profiles.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion between Aegean Prince, Valedictory, Dancing In Paris, Mountain Road, Synergism, and Ashnak all hunting the same early positions — expect significant bumping and checking 2-3f out on the final bend as the group compresses behind the lone front-runner Finalise.

Finalise's unchallenged lead risks producing a muddling, falsely-run tempo even on Heavy ground — if Marquand's pace is too conservative, the race could compress into a slow-motion sprint that negates the expected stamina test entirely.

In The Breeze is the clear stand-out on Heavy-ground win/place statistics but Ray Dawson rides him hold-up; from a large field on a testing surface, traffic through a congested midfield in the straight is a real threat to his chance.

Pole Star, Hermetic, and Kissmehoneyhoney are all natural prominent types who are likely to race out of their preferred position today — if one of them does manage to slot in early prominently, the style-fit discount lifts and their chance improves materially.

Aegean Prince's 320-day absence for Charlie Appleby and Godolphin is the biggest fitness question in the race — watch him in the paddock and at the start for any signs of edginess or race-ring rustiness before factoring his market position.

races.name: Betfair Sprint Cup Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almeraq
runners_data.note: A confirmed front-runner trained by William Haggas who has won or placed in three of eight runs on similar ground — his heavy-going credentials are the strongest in the field, but he faces a direct pace duel with two other confirmed leaders, and 56 days off the track raises a fitness query on this taxing surface.

runners_data.name: American Affair
runners_data.note: Jim Goldie's six-year-old has been in action just 15 days ago and has a win and two places from 15 runs on Soft — a solid prominent runner who is effective over 5-6f on easy ground but his form string showing a recent 0-2-0-6-1-0 sequence suggests inconsistency at this level.

runners_data.name: Aramram
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon's five-year-old has genuine prominent racing tendencies and two wins and three places from 15 runs on similar going, but in this pace-loaded field he will not be able to hold his natural pitch and is likely to find himself further back than ideal — the style fit discount is meaningful here.

runners_data.name: Big Mojo
runners_data.note: William Buick takes the ride on Michael Appleby's four-year-old, who won over this trip on Good ground but has just one run from 15 on anything near this going — his heavy-ground credentials are almost completely untested, which is a significant concern on the deepest ground in the card.

runners_data.name: James's Delight
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's five-year-old is a true prominent-type runner who has been pushed to the rear in the mapping because the field is overloaded with pace; his actual form — two wins and three places from 15 similar-going runs — is not to be ignored, but racing entirely against his instincts is a material disadvantage and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Kind Of Blue
runners_data.note: James Fanshawe's five-year-old has a win and a place from 14 runs on similar going and has been placed consistently at this trip, making him one of the more credible stamina-tested prominent types — however, a 77-day layoff on heavy ground is the key risk factor for James Doyle to manage.

runners_data.name: Marvelman
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's four-year-old is a confirmed front-runner who has operated mainly over 7f-8f on Soft and Good — dropping to 6f on heavy ground while simultaneously engaged in a three-way pace battle is a formidable ask, and his recent form (0-9-2-6-3) shows inconsistency, though he has placed on Soft.

runners_data.name: Paborus
runners_data.note: Daniel Tudhope rides Edward Bethell's five-year-old, who has a win and a place from nine runs on Soft/Standard and a strong recent record including back-to-back wins — his stamina over 6f-7f and willingness to race prominently make him one of the most interesting profiles if the front-runners destroy each other.

runners_data.name: Coppull
runners_data.note: The three-year-old trained by Clive Cox has won on Good ground at 6f and showed Group-race level form in a recent win, but has no run on heavy going and receives no weight allowance in this field at 129lbs — Hector Crouch will need her to secure a lead position or sit second from the three-way scramble, which is far from guaranteed.

races.paceDynamic: Almeraq, Marvelman, and Coppull are all confirmed front-runners, guaranteeing a fierce pace battle from the off over 6f on heavy ground at Haydock — a combination that will turn this into a severe stamina test at every stage. The three pace-setters will fight for positions from the stalls, creating a genuinely contested gallop that is unlikely to be anything less than maximum pressure, burning through the field by the time they reach the two-furlong pole. Prominent types American Affair, Big Mojo, Kind Of Blue, and Paborus will be compressed into a congested group just off the speed, creating significant traffic danger in the final two furlongs when tired horses drift and gaps close unpredictably. This race shape heavily favours the horse who can travel efficiently just off a suicidal pace and produce a sustained, grinding finish — a stamina-laden prominent or mid-division runner with proven heavy-ground credentials is the profile that benefits most. The field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural positions; of the redistributed horses, Aramram is a genuine prominent racer who will likely be squeezed back into midfield against his will, while James's Delight — also a true prominent type — is shown at the rear as the least pace-committed of an overcrowded group.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Stamina Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the three front-runners burn each other out in the first half, leaving the race to resolute finishers with proven stamina on heavy going.
scenarios.body: Almeraq, Marvelman, and Coppull set a scorching pace that proves catastrophic on deep Haydock ground, leaving them emptying inside the final two furlongs; horses who travel efficiently just behind the pace and grind out the closing stages dominate. Paborus, who has won on Soft/Standard and stays well, and Kind Of Blue, a consistent top-two finisher at this trip, are well-suited to collecting.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: One Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If one of the three front-runners — most likely Almeraq — breaks fastest, takes a clear lead, and sets a controlled rather than suicidal tempo.
scenarios.body: With rivals burning each other in a battle for second while the leader dictates from the front, the horse who secures the rail and a rhythm can prove uncatchable on stamina-sapping ground. Almeraq is the most obvious candidate given five wins or places from eight runs on similar going, and Coppull's course-and-distance form also warrants respect if she breaks sharply.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Profit
scenarios.trigger: If the pace battle is fierce enough to destroy the leaders but not so drawn-out that even mid-division runners close the gap, leaving those tracking just off the speed to benefit.
scenarios.body: American Affair and Big Mojo, both operating naturally in the prominent group, find the ideal racing position just behind a fast but controlled pace and pounce late; Marvelman, already blunted by the early duel, has no response. Big Mojo's lone heavy-going win is a thin sample but American Affair's record on Soft over 5f with proven finishing speed makes this profile credible if the pace collapses only partially.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is so extreme that the entire front half of the field capitulates, giving genuine hold-up horses a rare opportunity to sprint home late.
scenarios.body: James's Delight, though shown at the rear, is in truth a prominent racer who has been mapped there by redistribution rather than genuine hold-up instinct, meaning this scenario is structurally weakened by the absence of true closers. Aramram, similarly pushed back from his natural prominent position, is unlikely to get a clean passage even if the pace collapse is severe enough to theoretically suit late runners.

watchPoints.text: Almeraq, Marvelman, and Coppull will likely clash for the lead from the first stride — watch for a chaotic early split in the first furlong where any of the three fails to break cleanly and causes interference to the prominent group behind.

Prominent congestion between American Affair, Big Mojo, Kind Of Blue, and Paborus from the two-furlong pole is highly probable on this going — horses drifting under fatigue on heavy ground create real collision risk for any runner caught on a tiring shoulder.

Aramram is a genuine prominent-type who will be forced wider or further back than he wants — watch his early positioning because if he fails to find any rhythm in the first two furlongs his chance is effectively compromised regardless of ability.

Kind Of Blue's 77-day absence is notable on the most taxing ground of the season — watch how James Doyle settles him in the first quarter-mile, as a horse returning from that break who is not immediately comfortable on heavy going can be a traffic hazard to those around him.

Coppull is the youngest runner in the field (three-year-old, 129lbs) with zero heavy-ground exposure — watch her demeanour in the parade ring and her break from the stalls, as inexperience on this surface at Group 1 level can manifest immediately at the start.

races.name: Betfair Be Friendly Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Poatan
runners_data.note: Three-year-old hold-up performer for George Scott and David Egan who has form figures of 1-3 at 6f on soft/good-to-soft but trips on 5f on fast ground; heavy going is uncharted but his style of coming late should suit if the pace collapses.|

runners_data.name: Toyotomi
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's five-year-old was last out just six days ago, yet retains two career wins on soft/heavy-adjacent going at 6f and Daniel Tudhope's hold-up judgement at this track makes him dangerous if the pace fractions are taxing enough.|

runners_data.name: Arklow Lad
runners_data.note: Michael Appleby's four-year-old has genuine heavy-ground credentials and three wins on soft-equivalent going at 5f, and Clifford Lee will want to use his prominent style to track the leader from the first stride; 35 days off since his last run is the only query.|

runners_data.name: Advertised
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old for Grant Tuer who showed a placed effort on soft at 5f, though his remaining form is on good or quicker and one run in nine starts on similar ground is thin; prominent runner who may struggle to secure his natural berth if the early tempo is fierce.|

runners_data.name: Black Star Boy
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides this Ed Walker-trained three-year-old who landed a 5f win on good ground but whose five most recent efforts are all on fast surfaces and the heavy going here is a sharp, unproven step into the unknown for him.|

runners_data.name: Trilby
runners_data.note: PJ McDonald's partner has won twice on soft at 5f for Sam England and those form figures — 1/5f/SOF and 1/5f/SOF — are the most directly relevant in the field; the tongue-tie and cheekpieces combination has been in place throughout his good recent form and he is the horse best equipped to hold the prominent position he needs.|

runners_data.name: Sturlasson
runners_data.note: Stevie Donohoe takes the ride on this John Ryan-trained five-year-old who holds a placed run at 2/5f/GOO and one heavy-ground start — he races hold-up by style and will need significant pace collapse over 5f on this ground to reach the leaders.|

runners_data.name: Marching Mac
runners_data.note: Phil McEntee's five-year-old has two wins and five placed efforts on soft-adjacent going at 5f and is genuinely well-handicapped on that evidence, but his nature as a front-running/prominent type means he is more likely to be squeezed back into midfield by Trilby, Arklow Lad, and Advertised; his tongue-tie returns here and the style mismatch tempers confidence.|

runners_data.name: Elara May
runners_data.note: Philip McBride's three-year-old Hector Crouch rides has placed efforts on soft at 5f and 6f and is a natural prominent type who lacks the firepower to fight for that position against five rivals equally intent on tracking the leader — she will likely find herself racing a length or two further back than ideal and her chance is conditioned on what pace shape she ultimately gets.|

runners_data.name: Jer Batt
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner, raced yesterday for David & Nicola Barron which is a bold ask, but Ray Dawson knows the horse and his single heavy-ground run produced a fifth at 5f; he sets the tempo for everyone else and if allowed to stride clear uncontested he becomes relevant, but with four prominent types in his slipstream he is unlikely to get a soft lead.

races.paceDynamic: Jer Batt is the sole confirmed front-runner in a ten-horse field and, with just one day since his last run, Ray Dawson will need to press on immediately from the gates to establish position on the Haydock 5f straight. Behind him, Arklow Lad, Advertised, Black Star Boy, and Trilby all want prominent ground, creating a genuine scramble for the first two or three lengths of racing room, and that congestion will push early fractions higher than Jer Batt's lone-leader profile would otherwise produce. Marching Mac and Elara May are natural prominent types who are more likely to find themselves shuffled into midfield against their wishes, meaning the field holds more pace-hungry horses than the race shape can accommodate — Trilby and Arklow Lad, each with proven soft-ground form at 5f, are best placed to actually secure those prominent berths. On heavy Haydock ground over five furlongs, where the leader rarely gets it easy when a wall of prominent runners is in pursuit, the shape ultimately favours hold-up horses with heavy-ground class who can pick off tired rivals inside the final furlong — Poatan and Toyotomi sit in that bracket.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Holds On
scenarios.trigger: If Trilby or Arklow Lad slots in directly behind Jer Batt early and tracks the leader at a sustainable clip through the heavy ground.
scenarios.body: The prominent scrimmage settles quickly, Jer Batt sets an honest but not suicidal tempo, and the best-placed prominent runner has enough in reserve to overhaul the leader inside the final 100 yards; heavy ground rewards those who travel through it economically rather than those who chase hard from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early prominent battle is fierce enough to drain the leaders and genuine hold-up horses get a clear run in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Poatan and Toyotomi, sitting in the back half deliberately, find the pace has done enough damage to those in front that they can pick through tired rivals on the heavy ground; Toyotomi's two soft-ground wins at 6f and Poatan's ability to finish fast off a slow early crawl make them the logical beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Jer Batt is left completely uncontested and the prominent runners are slow away or get tangled in traffic.
scenarios.body: Jer Batt, who has run five career placed efforts at 5f including one on heavy, is given a soft lead and allowed to find a rhythm that saps the stamina of every pursuer on a deeply tiring surface; heavy ground places an enormous premium on conserving energy and any horse that has to burn fuel chasing from 3f out will struggle to close.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Claims It
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent scramble at the gates causes interference and several fancied runners are checked or lose their position.
scenarios.body: Racing becomes ragged and positional advantage becomes irrelevant; a lightly-exposed or forgotten runner such as Sturlasson, whose two recent placed efforts came on similar soft ground, could emerge from the carnage at a long price.

watchPoints.text: Prominent scramble danger: Trilby, Arklow Lad, Advertised, and Black Star Boy all want to race within two lengths of Jer Batt — watch the first two furlongs for contact and checking as they converge on limited rail space.|
Jer Batt ran yesterday and Ray Dawson must commit immediately to lead — any tardy start or hesitation could see him swamped before he has established his rhythm and the entire race shape unravels.|

Marching Mac and Elara May are likely to be pushed wider or further back than their trainers intend — if either finds a clear run hugging the rail they could improve markedly on what their map position suggests.|

Heavy going at Haydock on this straight 5f course is particularly stamina-sapping late on — horses who have hard-race records on soft or heavy and are near the top of the weights (Arklow Lad 133lbs, Advertised 133lbs) should be monitored for any sign of tiring quickly off the pace in the closing stages.|

Toyotomi runs just six days after his last outing and Sturlasson fifteen days — both are fresh enough, but Toyotomi's rapid turnaround for a hold-up horse on heavy ground means Tudhope's positional read in the early stages will be critical to whether he gets the run he needs.|

races.name: HKJC World Pool Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Brian
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with a recent second on soft/heavy-equivalent going at 7f; David Egan takes the ride for J S Moore who has limited recent form (1 win from 18 in 14 days), but Brian's heavy-ground profile is the most relevant asset here at this trip.

runners_data.name: Star Anthem
runners_data.note: Clive Cox's runner arrives just 28 days fresh and has form at 7f-8f on soft, though all five recent runs have come on good or soft/good and a true heavy test is an unknown quantity; Hector Crouch rides and this horse typically needs to be produced late.

runners_data.name: Korker
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up operator with a tendency to fade in the finish — the ⚠ flag is significant on heavy ground where the final furlong becomes a war of attrition; Clifford Lee partners him but recent form reads 0-8-0-6-4-8 and there is no heavy-ground win in his last 15 similar-going starts.

runners_data.name: Ata Rangi
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner here and likely to dictate; Tom Marquand for Ed Walker who has been in solid recent form (7 wins from 40 in 14 days), and Ata Rangi has placed on heavy going at this trip before — the style fit flag (0.92) reflects that racing up front is actually its natural role in this shape, not a departure from it.

runners_data.name: Cape Ashizuri
runners_data.note: Three-year-old by John & Sean Quinn's yard, arrives on the back of a win and a place at 6f on good, and is stepping up to 7f for the first time on heavy — the distance and ground combination are both unproven, but Marco Ghiani rides and the horse has strong recent form figures.

runners_data.name: Sergeant Wilko
runners_data.note: Kevin Ryan's 5-year-old is a genuine deep hold-up horse who will struggle to get his preferred rear position given how many closers populate this field; his best form has come on good-to-soft/good at 6f-7f and the step into heavy is not clearly in his favour, though P J McDonald is an experienced partner.

runners_data.name: Darkness
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's 8-year-old runs just 7 days after his last outing, wears a visor, and has six consecutive finishes of 6th or worse — a horse firmly out of form whose hold-up style means he will be shuffled back into a traffic queue with several rivals chasing the same late ground on testing going.

runners_data.name: Brighton Boy
runners_data.note: Tim Easterby's 4-year-old is back quickly (14 days) and carries a hood; his best form figures at 6f on soft are encouraging for the conditions, but he is a true closer who will sit deep in the pack as the field stacks up — Jake Dickson claims 5lb which helps on the weights.

runners_data.name: Rhoscolyn
runners_data.note: An 8-year-old who wears a tongue-tie and has a finish-fading flag, having placed on soft at 7f, though more recent efforts are poor; David Tudhope's experience helps, but running 5 days ago is a quick turnaround on heavy ground and genuine late runs have dried up of late.

runners_data.name: Montezin
runners_data.note: Antony Brittain's 4-year-old is the only horse other than Ata Rangi likely to race prominently; he won at 7f on good and has shown consistent placed form, wears a tongue-strap and cheekpieces, and if he can track the leader without getting into a duel, he represents the major threat to Ata Rangi's supremacy at the weights.

runners_data.name: Wreck It Ryley
runners_data.note: Alan Brown's 6-year-old wears blinkers and is a hold-up horse who placed at 6f on soft; the trainer has no wins from 6 runners in the past 14 days and this horse's recent form string (3-8-9-6-3-7) shows inconsistency — placed into midfield by the traffic map, his true instinct is to race from the rear.

runners_data.name: King Of Thunder
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's 3-year-old is the most lightly raced runner here, returning after a 121-day absence, and his only win came on soft at 7f — the fitness question is real but the going profile is relevant; a hold-up type who will be held up deep, he represents interest if he comes back fit.

races.paceDynamic: Ata Rangi is the lone confirmed front-runner and, on heavy ground at Haydock over 7f, is likely to bowl along at a measured but relentless gallop with little genuine pressure from rivals — this is a single-paced, grinding tempo rather than a frantically contested lead. Montezin is the only other prominent type capable of tracking up and providing any semblance of first-run pressure, but the remainder of the field is dominated by hold-up horses who must come from off the pace. The field does, however, hold far more hold-up types than the track map can accommodate: Sergeant Wilko, Darkness, Brighton Boy, Rhoscolyn, Wreck It Ryley and King Of Thunder are all genuine rear-of-field horses who cannot all get their natural position; in practice the majority will be stacked in midfield rather than truly hunting their preferred late berth. On heavy ground over 7f at Haydock, a controlled front-running gallop set by one horse tends to be sustainable rather than suicidal, meaning the race shape firmly favours hold-up types who possess genuine heavy-ground stamina and can make late ground — but with so many closers crowding the same tactical space, the premium falls on those with the cleanest trajectory and proven soft/heavy-ground credentials.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Ata Rangi Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Ata Rangi dictates an uncontested, steady heavy-ground gallop and rivals cannot close on the testing surface.
scenarios.body: Ata Rangi sets its own rhythm from the front with Montezin tracking, and the grinding heavy going plays to a horse that has previously placed at 7f on heavy; hold-up horses expend energy to close ground they never fully recover.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Closers Grind Through
scenarios.trigger: If the heavy ground gradually slows the pace enough that genuine hold-up horses with soft/heavy form pick off the front two in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The relentless effort on testing ground chips away at Ata Rangi's lead inside the final two furlongs, and the horses with the best heavy/soft credentials and racing room come through.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Montezin presses Ata Rangi from early, sets a true honest gallop, and both hold on as hold-up horses fail to get home in the mud.
scenarios.body: With two horses running prominent on extreme going, the closers — many of whom lack genuine heavy-ground form or are crowded together in midfield — cannot sustain their finishing effort over the final half furlong.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos — Midfield Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed midfield bunch creates traffic problems and a surprise hold-up type finds daylight late at a big price.
scenarios.body: With six or more horses all hunting the same late ground in a condensed pack, a less-fancied runner finds an uncontested rail or outer run and collects.

watchPoints.text: Ata Rangi leads uncontested — watch whether Tom Marquand is able to control the tempo completely; if he gets a soft lead on heavy ground with no rival willing to press, the race could be over turning for home.

The midfield cluster of Sergeant Wilko, Darkness, Brighton Boy, Rhoscolyn, Wreck It Ryley and King Of Thunder will create serious traffic congestion from 3f out — watch for any horse finding a clean outside run, as that alone could be decisive.

Cape Ashizuri steps up to 7f for the first time on heavy going — watch the market move at the off; if connections are confident about the trip and ground combination, the form figures at 6f suggest she could be underestimated.

Darkness and Rhoscolyn both ran within the last 7 days — watch their early behaviour and whether the quick turnaround on extreme ground affects their finishing effort, particularly given both already carry fading-in-finish flags.

King Of Thunder returns after 121 days off — watch his pre-race condition and early market move; Hugo Palmer runners returning from long breaks at Haydock on heavy are worth monitoring as fitness is a genuine variable here.

races.name: Betfair.Betfair Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Yanifer
runners_data.note: 8yo prominent runner with headgear, 140lbs top weight is a significant burden on heavy ground; best sim-going form shows 1W3P from 6 runs but all those efforts were at 7f, and this 8f trip may stretch stamina under these conditions at her age.

runners_data.name: Metal Merchant
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with solid heavy-ground profile (OK tag confirmed); Sean Levey booking is noteworthy, 137lbs is manageable, and the 24-day freshener suits; best suited if the contested pace creates a genuine test of stamina in the straight.

runners_data.name: Final Night
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent runner with excellent recent form (236022) and an experienced David Egan booking; all five recent runs at 8f gives strong trip confidence, though sim-going record (1/15, 0W0P) suggests heavy ground may blunt his finishing effort.

runners_data.name: Military Leader
runners_data.note: In excellent form with four consecutive top-three finishes including a recent win; headgear (blinkers) applied, Paul Mulrennan rides, and two placed efforts on soft give confidence at this level — the profile of a horse ready to capitalise from a prominent position if the pace is honest.

runners_data.name: Caim
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner with strong similar-going form (3/4, 1W2P); Daniel Tudhope is a top-class booking and the 3yo has already won on soft over a mile, but must deal with Crown Office for the early lead which will drain energy on this testing surface.

runners_data.name: Miletus
runners_data.note: Prominent runner with headgear (tongue-tie, blinkers); 36-day break is notable but trainer has only 1/1 in the 14-day window which is a small sample; best form at 7f (won at 7f Good), and this heavy-ground mile represents a step into uncharted territory on the going.

runners_data.name: Jungle Ruler
runners_data.note: 3yo prominent runner who has struggled to convert form (0W in recent 5); all recent runs on Good or Soft-Good, so heavy ground is an unproven question; Clifford Lee rides and the 38-day absence adds a fitness query in a competitive handicap.

runners_data.name: Crown Office
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner trained by William Haggas, excellent yard in form (11/52 T14); won on soft at 6f and placed at 10f Good, so the trip and conditions are not an obvious negative — must fight for the lead with Caim, which risks burning both horses on this ground.

runners_data.name: Monoceros
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse for Iain Jardine; all recent form on Good ground with only one run on Soft (placed), so heavy ground is the biggest question mark; Andrew Mullen's claim could help with weight but the going concern is real for this 3yo.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: In excellent winning form (461121) with three recent victories at 8f including on soft, and headgear (tongue-tie) aids; races prominently by nature but cannot secure that position in this congested field — will be pushed wider into midfield, which is not where this horse performs best and tempers the chance meaningfully.

runners_data.name: Bearin Up
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse dropping back from 10f trips to 8f, which is a question, though Tim Easterby sends out plenty of winners (10/83 T14); only 15-day turnaround after a 0 finishing position is worth noting — heavy ground may not be a concern but the trip shortening and that recent blank are flags.

runners_data.name: Kindest Nation
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse who wears a visor (headgear noted); Hugo Palmer runner with only 2/29 in the 14-day window; sim-going record (4/15, 0W1P) is modest but the style is perfect if the race is run as a thorough test of stamina — Joe Leavy's claim helps offset the weight.

races.paceDynamic: Caim and Crown Office are the two confirmed front-runners and will fight for the early lead down Haydock's straight mile on heavy ground, creating a genuine contested pace from the off rather than a false gallop. With five horses wanting prominent positions — Yanifer, Final Night, Military Leader, Miletus, and Jungle Ruler — the early stages will be congested and physical, likely burning energy reserves at a premium in conditions that punish wasteful horses. The pace pressure created by two genuine lead types slugging it out on heavy ground at a mile typically sets it up for those who can sit just off the pace and pick up late, meaning the hold-up horses and the strongest stayers in this field should benefit most. The Sweet Escape is a genuine prominent runner who cannot realistically hold that position in this shape and has been mapped to midfield, with Caim and Crown Office almost certain to dominate the front rank ahead of the congested prominent pack.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Closers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Caim and Crown Office burn each other up through a genuine pace battle on heavy ground, setting the race up for those tracking or coming from off the pace.
scenarios.body: The two front-runners exhaust themselves on energy-sapping heavy ground, leaving the prominent pack also compromised by early congestion, allowing fresher horses to reel in the leaders in the straight. True hold-up types and sit-and-wait horses who can conserve energy and pick their moment benefit most in this shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Delivered Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong but not suicidal, allowing horses in the prominent-to-midfield group to travel kindly and produce a finish without being compromised by the early battle.
scenarios.body: Horses like Military Leader and Final Night, who are proven at this trip and have strong recent form, would be in the ideal position to pounce without having burned their tanks leading. Military Leader's consistent placed form at 8f on soft-ish ground makes him the standout profile here.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Leader Kicks Clear Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If one of the two front-runners — most likely Caim — gets a soft lead by outpacing Crown Office early and controls from the front without being pressed.
scenarios.body: Caim has strong similar-going form (3/4 runs in sim conditions, 1W 2P) and a strong jockey booking in Tudhope, and if Crown Office drops back quickly Caim could dictate a manageable tempo on heavy ground and prove hard to catch. The 3yo has already won over a mile on soft and has course-applicable form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is truly extreme and the entire field is strung out, allowing a patient late-closer to charge through beaten rivals in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Bearin Up and Monoceros are the truest hold-up types in this field, but both carry concerns — Bearin Up drops back from 10f trips and Monoceros has limited heavy-ground evidence. The scenario is possible but relies on horses with unproven stamina or form profiles at this trip and going.

watchPoints.text: Caim and Crown Office will fight for the front — watch the first two furlongs to see if one capitulates early, as whoever blinks first defines the entire race shape for 12 runners.

Military Leader has had four consecutive placed efforts and is visually in the form of his life — if he gets a clean position from the gate without being pushed wide by the prominent congestion, he is the standout pace-scenario beneficiary.

The Sweet Escape is racing out of natural role in a congested prominent group — watch for traffic issues 2-3f out if pushed wide or squeezed into a pocket in midfield, which would be costly at this short price relative to recent form.
Bearin Up's last run reads as a 0 (last of finishers) just 15 days ago — watch the market move and Fentiman's early positioning to gauge whether connections are confident the horse has bounced back.

Heavy ground on a straight mile at Haydock tests pure stamina late; watch which horses are off the bridle earliest turning into the final two furlongs, as the energy cost of the early contested pace may see several prominent runners emptying simultaneously in the final 150 yards.
